title: Exact DeWitt kernels in Lorentzian quantum cosmology
abstract: The DeWitt boundary condition can be implemented in the Lorentzian path integral of minisuperspace quantum cosmology by summing only over non-singular paths. We give a general definition of the resulting DeWitt kernels, together with explicit rules for constructing them, and evaluate them exactly. The lapse integral over the positive half-line yields the Dirichlet Green function of the Wheeler--DeWitt operator, whereas the integral over the whole real line yields the Dirichlet group-averaging kernel; both vanish when either endpoint lies at the singularity. Since the minisuperspace actions are at most quadratic, all lapse integrals are performed in closed form without saddle-point approximations. We obtain the kernels for the closed universe without cosmological constant, where the whole-real-line kernel vanishes identically, for the flat de Sitter universe, and, in terms of Airy functions, for the closed and open de Sitter universes. Throughout, the DeWitt condition is imposed as the boundary condition at the singularity, which selects a self-adjoint constraint operator on the half-line and fixes the kernels uniquely, including their normalization.
summary: This paper provides a rigorous, exact calculation of DeWitt kernels for quantum cosmology by implementing the DeWitt boundary condition in the Lorentzian path integral. It establishes general construction rules and derives explicit kernel forms for various cosmological models, confirming the consistency between different mathematical approaches for defining quantum propagators in constrained systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the technical challenge of correctly implementing the DeWitt boundary condition within the Lorentzian path integral formulation of minisuper-space quantum cosmology.
main_result: The authors provide general definitions and exact construction rules for DeWitt kernels, yielding explicit, closed-form expressions for these kernels in various cosmological backgrounds (e.g., de Sitter space).
method: The methodology involves using the Batalin–Fradkin–Vilkovisky (BFV) path integral approach, analyzing lapse integrals over different contours (positive half-line vs. whole real line), and imposing the DeWitt condition as a boundary constraint.
model_or_system: The physical system is minisuper-space quantum cosmology, governed by a constraint operator derived from the metric $ds^2 = \sigma^2 (-N^2 q dt^2 + q d\Omega^2)$. The dynamics are described by the Wheeler–DeWitt equation.
key_observables: The DeWitt kernels, specifically the positive-lapse kernel ($G^+$) and the whole-real-line kernel ($G_R$), are the primary observables.
important_parameters: The cosmological constant ($\Lambda$), the scale factor variable ($q$), and the boundary condition parameter ($\alpha$) are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to a single self-adjoint constraint operator with the flat measure $dN$, neglecting full gauge fixing and Faddeev–Popov measures.
paper_structure: The paper develops the general framework for constructing DeWitt kernels, derives specific forms for the positive-lapse and whole-real-line kernels, and then applies these general results to calculate exact kernels for specific cosmological models like the closed, flat, and open de Sitter universes.
why_interesting: While focused on cosmology, the rigorous mathematical techniques for defining propagators via path integrals over gauge degrees of freedom (the lapse $N$) and handling boundary conditions (like the Dirichlet condition) are highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum field theory in curved spacetime.
